title: Persist strictly allowlisted analytics events
input: analytics-consent-api, shared event schemas and the published-product source
accept: 1) Through HTTP with a valid signed-consent cookie, separately send page_view/product_view/model_view_start/model_load_success/model_load_failure/chat_start. Assert required navigationId/viewId/productSlug, the published-product allowlist and strict length boundaries individually. Reject forged/unpublished products, unknown kinds, oversized fields and full URLs with sensitive query parameters; rejected events do not increase the row count. Rate-limit the 121st event per cookie per minute or the 301st event per IP-HMAC per minute under section 10, returning 429 with Retry-After and persisting no rejected events. Query raw-event fields to verify no raw IP, cross-site fingerprint, email, chat body or sensitive full URL is stored (E-47). 2) PostgreSQL stores only one row for repeated eventId/semanticKey with the same payload and returns 409 for differing payloads. The same viewId has only one success/failure terminal; product-page events and start/terminal records are stored separately, and failure does not write success. Reject timestamps outside -48h/+5min. 3) After consent-cookie withdrawal, requests return 403 and event-row count does not change. M2-T7 wires the client model producer; M5-T7 wires browser consent and ordinary-page producers.

title: Wire consent UI, page events and privacy explanations
input: analytics-consent-api, analytics-ingest, client-api-foundation and the existing footer preferences entry; the public time zone from analytics-settings-domain and existing en/ru privacy copy
output: analytics-consent-ui and analytics-page-events; serialized consent writes and page producers; analytics-privacy-copy privacy-page and anonymous-browser/retention explanations
accept: 1) In a blank browser context click footer analytics-preferences and assert the preferences panel is visible. In both the unselected and Reject-clicked states, cookies/browser storage contain no analytics identity, the POST /api/analytics/events count is 0, and product navigation/model controls still respond to clicks. Clicking Allow sends analytics=true to POST /api/analytics/consent and receives a valid signed cookie. Subsequent navigation produces page_view with this eventId in response acceptedIds; retrying the same navigationId leaves exactly one database row (E-42). 2) Disconnect the network before event transmission to create a pending queue, then click Withdraw: local analytics identity and pending-item count both become 0, and reconnecting sends none of that queue. Further navigation sends no events; the cookie is cleared, and an old pending-event request without a valid cookie after clearing returns 403. Separately delay the actual true-request response, then click false; assert serialized writes with false last, and after all responses the cookie is absent, the queue is 0 and collection does not resume. Do not backfill withdrawn-period visits (E-43). 3) At 1920x1080, 1440x900 and 390x844 retain request/interaction GIFs. Computed border width equals 2px, border radius equals 0px and accent color equals the section 11 token. Tab focuses each named control, Enter/Space operates it and each measured touch target is at least 44 CSS px. 4) Click footer privacy-link to /[locale]/privacy. The en definition contains anonymous browsers that consented to analytics, and the ru definition contains анонимных браузеров, разрешивших аналитику. Copy makes no unique-real-person/cross-device-identification claim. Isolated tests separately change device contexts, clear identifiers and switch browsers; query the backend to verify a new browserHash can form while reporting only whether it differs, not its raw value (E-45). 5) Necessary-chat, analytics-consent and cleanup-state sections are each visible on the privacy page. Retention displays configuration values: chat cookie seven days idle/30 days absolute, consultation 90 days, raw analytics 30 days/aggregates 13 months; the site-IANA text equals SiteSetting. Default cleanup state explicitly shows disabled/dry-run and that actual cleanup requires separate authorization, without treating documents/dispatch as authorization. robots/noindex still follows the existing completeness switch.

title: Register the aggregation job and wire real five-minute cron
input: job-leases, analytics-aggregate and shared M3 HTTP protections
output: job-foundation and analytics-aggregate-runtime; a fixed registry, POST /api/admin/cron/operations and real cron
accept: 1) composition registers only the implemented analytics-aggregate; deploy/cron.nbshiyan calls POST /api/admin/cron/operations every five minutes. Validate fixed keys/Bearer credentials in constant time; reject unknown keys/missing credentials and permit no arbitrary scripts. 2) Real scheduling executes after restart and commits JobState/watermark, with batch at most 500, a 55s deadline and no old-generation overwrite. Stopped cron/failure preserves the last successful watermark and exposes safe NEVER/FAILED/stale-value state; route existence/manual invocation does not justify claiming just updated (E-81, E-84). 3) After browser consent, complete two same-day page visits in the same browser and refresh/retry the same eventId. After the actual job UV stays 1, genuine new visits increase PV and duplicate events do not increase counts (E-44). Dashboard GET does not trigger jobs; M4 registers notification/mail jobs, without future-service imports or empty implementations. 4) In an isolated service with a controlled clock, use the event HTTP entry to submit now-48h-1ms, now-48h, now+5min and now+5min+1ms separately. The two out-of-range inputs return event_time_out_of_range without records, while both exact boundaries can be admitted. An admitted future event is excluded until the actual aggregation-job clock reaches its occurredAt, and counted only afterward. Events arriving within 48h recompute only their day when complete raw coverage remains; arbitrary client timestamps cannot contaminate closed/out-of-window history. Beyond complete coverage preserve the original aggregate and mark partial/unavailable, without reducing counts from fragments or fabricating future days (E-60).
